---
title: "The Unified Table"
---

Every method in the book on one page, one row per method, with the columns of the method cards
plus what each method changed relative to the one it modifies. The rows are generated from a single
data file (`scripts/method_data.py`), transcribed from the method cards in the chapters, so the
table and the chapters say the same thing. Each method's name links to the chapter where its card
is derived. "Undisclosed" marks fields of RLCD that TypeSafe AI has not published.

Type in the box to filter rows (for example "verifiable", "offline", "critic", "token").

```{=html}
<input id="ut-filter" type="search" placeholder="Filter methods…" aria-label="Filter the unified table"
       style="width:100%;max-width:420px;padding:6px 10px;margin:4px 0 12px;border:1px solid #d8d6cf;border-radius:4px;font:inherit">
<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  var box = document.getElementById("ut-filter");
  var table = document.querySelector("main table");
  if (!box || !table) return;
  box.addEventListener("input", function () {
    var q = box.value.toLowerCase();
    table.querySelectorAll("tbody tr").forEach(function (tr) {
      tr.style.display = tr.textContent.toLowerCase().indexOf(q) === -1 ? "none" : "";
    });
  });
});
</script>
```

::: {.column-page}
{{< include includes/unified-table-full.md >}}
:::

Two reading notes. A method "targets $\pi^\star$" only in the idealized sense of the
[shared-target chapter](chapters/06-the-shared-target.qmd): with enough data, a policy that can
represent it, and the KL implemented as in that chapter. And "fully on-policy" methods are, in
practice, slightly off-policy wherever they reuse a batch for several updates.
